transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start: 16:00 PT | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Jane Kim (Veridian Head of ML), Omar Singh (Infra), Priya Rao (PM)

--- Auto Summary (auto-generated; may be incomplete) ---
Redwood and Veridian confirmed POC acceptance metrics. Action items include runbook share, VPC peering and schedule. Agreed 2-week benchmark window with weekly sync and final sign-off.

--- Topics ---
1) Acceptance thresholds
2) Benchmark plan and dataset sizing
3) Reporting schema and cadence
4) Security/network constraints
5) Timeline and signoff process

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Lena: okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time today. quick agenda — finalize the acceptance thresholds and the reporting format so when we start the bench it's, it's clear how we decide go/no-go.
00:18 Jane: thanks lena, yeah we've got the eval set ready, um 200 canonical items and then a larger sample pool — our main concerns are latency for user-facing flows and cost for bulk back-office tasks.
00:34 Marco: great, do you have target concurrency and average prompt length? that'll shape kernel selection and batching configs.
00:42 Jane: average prompt is about 350 tokens, peak concurrency 120 qps in the worst case, sustained 40 qps. sometimes we have longer generative flows up to 1k tokens but that's rarer.
00:58 Omar: just to flag infra constraints: traffic must stay within our eu-west region and keys must use our KMS, also we need VPC peering, no public internet egress for the payloads.
01:12 Lena: we can support region controls and customer-managed KMS, and private peering is supported in Dedicated and Private — for the hosted POC we can set up VPC peering to our test tenancy.
01:28 Priya: timeline wise we want a sign-off within three weeks; ideally 2 if everything's green.
01:35 Marco: ok on thresholds — we usually propose goal & pass/fail thresholds. example for user-facing: goal latency p95 <= 220ms for a 350-token prompt; pass threshold p95 < 280ms. does that align?
01:49 Jane: 220 p95 would be amazing but our product team wants to see 95th < 300ms as minimum. so your goal sounds fine but pass must be under 300ms.
02:02 Lena: cool — we'll record both: goal p95 220ms, pass p95 300ms. for throughput: target sustained 40 qps with CPU/GPU utilization under 80% and no dropped requests.
02:15 Marco: for batch and KV caching, we'll run three model variants: base instruct model (r-instruct-v2), quantized int8 variant, and a smaller 7B fallback. we will run each under three traffic profiles: steady 40qps, spiky 120qps bursts, and long-tail 1k token cases (low qps).
02:34 Jane: what about quality? we need pass rate on the 200 canonical eval items — goal 94% accuracy, pass 90% (allowing some tolerance for ambiguous prompts).
02:47 Priya: how do you define accuracy — exact match or semantic?
02:52 Marco: semantic judgement by rubric — the customer will provide tags and acceptance criteria per item. our report will include per-item judgement and aggregate pass rate. we'll also compute BLEU/ROUGE as supplemental but not primary.
03:06 Lena: cost thresholds — customer asked for a cost baseline. we'll include estimated per-1M-token cost for each variant. do you have a budget cap?
03:16 Jane: we want an estimate, not a hard cap; but anything above $15 per 1M tokens for generative workloads will be tough for ops to justify.
03:24 Marco: noted. we'll include cost modeled from measured tokens/sec and our price matrix.
03:31 Omar: on reporting format — we need a CSV with specific columns: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, prompt_tokens, generated_tokens, latency_ms (p50,p95 recorded per minute), status (success|error), error_type, cost_estimate, eval_pass (if in eval set), region. also a summary sheet with aggregated metrics and confidence intervals.
03:57 Lena: yes, sample report will be a CSV and an Excel pivot summary. we'll attach the sample in the runbook.
04:05 Jane: what about sampling frequency — we don't need per-request for long runs, minute granularity is fine but for troubleshooting we want raw logs for a 1% sample.
04:16 Marco: we'll capture full traces for 1% sample with traces and KV cache hit ratios. note transcription: our KV 'cash' wording — sorry, kv cache.
04:25 Lena: ha, ok noted.
04:28 Priya: security checklist — SOC2, SSO, audit logs. we already got SOC2 escrows but need details on retention and if Redwood provides audit log exports.
04:39 Lena: Redwood provides audit logs and you can configure retention; for private deployments you can push logs to your SIEM via Kinesis or S3. we'll include a security pack.
04:48 Omar: we need to validate encryption in transit and at rest and ensure no model snapshots are stored in our tenancy outside the permitted bucket.
04:57 Marco: acknowledged, we'll document KMS envelope flow.
05:02 Lena: back to acceptance: let's enumerate go/no-go gates — if any gate fails we go to remediation window 5 business days, then a re-run. gates: 1) Latency gate = p95 under 300ms (pass) 2) Quality gate = aggregate pass rate >= 90% on canonical set 3) Throughput gate = sustain 40qps without >5% error rate 4) Cost gate = estimated per-1M tokens <= $20 (pass) — goal targets will be tighter for scoring.
05:32 Jane: can we make cost pass $15 not $20? ops will push back.
05:36 Lena: we'll make the pass threshold configurable in the report; by default we'll aim for $15 and if we can't get there we'll show delta and suggested config (quantization, batching) to meet target.
05:50 Marco: for reporting cadence — daily summary, immediate alert if p95 breaches pass threshold by >20% for a 1h rolling window, and full benchmark PDF at end of run.
06:02 Priya: who signs off? I need legal and product and infra. I'll send the list.
06:07 Jane: product+infra signoff, if both green Priya will do final sign-off.
06:12 Lena: perfect. I'll include a signoff template in the runbook.
06:16 Omar: one more infra question — are we running in Redwood Dedicated or hosted trial environment? we may need dedicated nodes to reach the higher concurrency.
06:24 Marco: for the POC we can run in a dedicated trial pool we spin up for 2 weeks; that'll mimic production. if not available, we'll emulate load in hosted with throttling but real performance may differ.
06:36 Lena: ok action items recap then — I'll send runbook and sample CSV, Marco will prep model variants, Omar to finish peering, Jane to share eval set, Priya to share signoff list.
06:52 Jane: quick clarification — the canonical eval set is in S3, we'll create IAM role and a read-only key for Redwood. is that sufficient?
07:01 Omar: yes we prefer role-based access, do not share long-lived keys.
07:05 Marco: we'll consume via secure connector and respect region residency.
07:11 Priya: anything else on timelines?
07:14 Lena: proposed timeline in bullet below — share-runbook by 11/05, infra ready by 11/09, integration slot on 11/10, baseline run 11/11-11/13, results review 11/16, final run and signoff 11/20. if everything passes earlier we can compress.
07:36 Jane: sounds good.
07:38 Lena: cool, thanks all. we'll email the artifacts and next steps. end.

--- End of transcript ---

Notes on noisy transcription: there are a few small mis-recognitions of product names and acronyms (e.g., "KV cash"), and speaker overlaps are minimized. The transcript includes the core acceptance thresholds and agreed runbook timing.
